Action Plan:
1. Begin ibuprofen 400 mg orally twice daily after food for anti-inflammatory relief of left elbow swelling; stop if heartburn or other adverse effects occur.
2. Mail patient laboratory request forms for: CBC, ESR/CRP, rheumatoid factor/anti-CCP, ANA profile, serum urate, and basic metabolic panel; patient to attend phlebotomy service as instructed.
3. Schedule follow-up review (video or in-person per patient preference) approximately 6 days after blood draw to examine elbow and review results.
4. Provide red-flag advice: if elbow becomes very red, increasingly painful, or redness spreads, contact service urgently for same-day assessment to exclude septic arthritis.
5. Encourage continued usual activity as tolerated; avoid prolonged direct pressure on elbow.
6. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
• Reason for visit: New swelling over left elbow noticed ~1 week ago.  
• HPI: Painless or minimally tender mass; mild warmth; no marked redness; full range of motion; no trauma recalled; first episode.  
• Past medical history: Osteoarthritis (GP-diagnosed, several years ago).  
• Allergies: Peanuts (food). No known drug allergies.  
• Medications: None routinely.  
• Social history: Desk-based job; runs 2–3 ×/week; otherwise well.

Objective:
• Video examination – left elbow:  
  – Visible localized swelling over olecranon.  
  – Overlying skin mildly warm; slight tenderness adjacent to tip.  
  – Skin over tip appears dry.  
  – Full active ROM; no erythema, no obvious joint effusion.  
• No vitals provided. No systemic signs noted.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Left elbow swelling
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Aseptic (non-infectious) olecranon bursitis (DDx item: “Aseptic olecranon bursitis” – High likelihood).
   - Differential diagnosis:
     • Septic olecranon bursitis – Medium (warmth/tenderness but no systemic signs).  
     • Gouty olecranon bursitis – Medium-Low (age/sex fit; urate test ordered).  
     • Post-traumatic bursitis/hematoma – Low (denies trauma).  
     • Soft-tissue tumor – Low (acute onset, warmth argue against).
   - Investigations planned: CBC, ESR/CRP, rheumatoid antibodies, ANA, serum urate, ± basic metabolic panel (forms to be mailed).
   - Treatment planned: Ibuprofen 400 mg PO BID after food; patient to stop if dyspepsia.
   - Relevant referrals: Follow-up consultation (video or face-to-face) ~1 week post-testing for clinical reassessment and result review; escalate to urgent care if red-flag symptoms develop.

Quality checks:
• Missing expected elements: No vital signs recorded; smoking/alcohol status not elicited; complete medication/allergy reconciliation adequate.  
• Internal conflicts: None noted between transcript and DDx.  
• Transcript quality: Clear audio; occasional minor omissions but clinical content intact.
